verdict.rationale: Several pieces point toward scope reduction. Checkout.com lets you request payments with a token or network token instead of full card details. It offers client-side public keys and hosted or low-code options (Hosted Payment Page, Flow), marketed as helping you "stay compliant" with "no confusing compliance". However, no evidence explicitly says card data bypasses merchant servers or names a reduced PCI DSS scope. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that client-side tokenization keeps raw PANs off merchant servers, PCI DSS scope/SAQ guidance (e.g., SAQ A eligibility), independent or hands-on corroboration.
